answer: Agents deter Sybil attacks by anchoring identities to acoustic telemetry across a coastal reef. Candidate nodes transmit phase-locked pulses using a discrete copper transducer, which verifiers decode over a trellis graph to confirm unique spatial coordinates. Adversaries cannot virtualize nodes because each identity requires dedicated submerged hardware and local deployment costs. However, dynamic thermoclines alter sound velocity, causing intermittent false rejections.
